newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRA's "nightmare" route to Irish unity - Bruton.
newsitem.headline: IRA's "nightmare" route to Irish unity - Bruton.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton assailed IRA guerrillas on Monday for violently pursuing "a nightmare version" of Irish unity which ignored the rights of Northern Ireland's pro-British majority Protestants.

Bruton, named European of the Year by the Irish Council of the European Movement, also told reporters he had agreed to meet Catholics who want Britain to re-open a probe into army shootings of 13 unarmed nationalists in Londonderry city in 1972.

Last month Ireland urged Britain to examine new evidence about the "Bloody Sunday" killings which the victims' relatives say were unprovoked. Britain promises to look at any fresh information but has refused to apologise for the killings.

Bruton, whose government held the six-monthly rotated presidency of the European Union until the end of 1996, lambasted Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland. He said peace would win out.
The Republican Movement, which comprises the IRA and its Sinn Fein political arm, "continues to kill people for political ends," Bruton said.
He was speaking five days after the guerrillas were widely blamed for a sniper attack that killed a British soldier.
IRA-style republicanism "in its pursuit of its nightmarish version of unity, does not respect the rule of law. It uses force wherever and whenever it suits," Bruton said after receiving the award.
"Its territorial concept of unity allows one nation, one flag, and one allegiance alone, to be recognised on the unilaterally defined national territory," Bruton said.
History was on the side of the peacemaker in Ireland just as it was on the side of the builders of European unity, he said. "We can and will have peace on this island."

The IRA says Britain should give Sinn Fein a seat in peace talks but a recent wave of guerrilla attacks has outraged government leaders in London and Dublin who demand an end to violence as the price of a Sinn Fein place at the table.
